method: Critical swim speed is the slope of the distance-time line through two maximal trials: CSS = (400 - 200) / (T400 - T200) in metres or yards per second, with both times in seconds. The page reports that speed, the equivalent pace per 100 as 100 / CSS, which is also exactly (T400 - T200) / 2 seconds, the average pace of each trial, the distance reserve D' = 400 - CSS x T400 (the part of the 400 that stored work covered rather than the sustainable rate), and a table of pace and repetition time at 70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 100, 105 and 110 percent of CSS speed, where pace = CSS pace / (percent / 100) and repetition time = distance / speed. Times are entered as minutes:seconds or whole seconds, must fall between 1:00 and 1:00:00, the 400 must be the longer swim, and the resulting speed must fall between 0.3 and 2.5 units per second; a 200 faster than half the 400 time (a negative distance reserve) or a 400 more than 2.5 times the 200 time is reported as a caution. The protocol is fixed at 400 and 200, in metres or yards. Critical swim speed is a model of the sustainable rate: swimmers usually hold it for tens of minutes rather than indefinitely, pacing errors in either trial shift it, and 25 m and 50 m pools give different values. It is a training aid, not a lab measurement or medical advice, and everything is computed in the browser with no uploads, network access or storage.

sources.title: Wakayoshi K, Ikuta K, Yoshida T, et al. Determination and validity of critical velocity as an index of swimming performance in the competitive swimmer. European Journal of Applied Physiology and Occupational Physiology, 1992;64(2):153-157.
MacKenzie B. Critical Swim Speed: test protocol and how the resulting speed sets training times. BrianMac Sports Coach, 2003.
